Subject: High error rate on dedicated GPU pool — immediate assistance required

Connor —

We started seeing elevated 5xx errors and sustained request latency for our Dedicated pool (pool-id: bc-ded-77) starting ~07:55 PT. Traffic is normal from our side; autoscaling didn't appear to add extra nodes and several requests failed with "capacity_exceeded" in the last 20 minutes. Throughput dropped ~40% for inference jobs.

We can provide logs if useful, but need immediate guidance: can you route our production traffic to a hosted fallback while you stabilize the pool? We are in the middle of a campaign and this is customer-impacting.

Attached: brief error-snapshot (logs.csv) and a short HAR export.

Thanks —
Alice Nguyen
SRE, BrightCommerce

Subject: Re: High error rate on dedicated GPU pool — immediate assistance required

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the alert and the artifacts. I'm looking at the pool now. Initial triage shows the autoscaler did not provision extra reserved nodes due to a transient quota-check timeout against our scheduler; the runtime kept queueing requests and rejected some when per-node token budgets were exhausted.

Immediate options (short list):
- Temporary routing: we can route your traffic to a hosted-compatible variant (same model family, slightly lower qps headroom) while we restore dedicated capacity (expected 20–45 minutes).
- Manual warm-up: our ops team can manually bring up two standby nodes in the pool to buy time (~15 minutes).

Action I will take now: 1) open an internal incident and escalate to infra-ops; 2) initiate temporary routing if you give the go-ahead; 3) share an internal mitigation playbook and ETA.

Can you confirm whether you want the traffic routed now or prefer us to attempt manual warm-up first? If routing, please confirm that your application tolerates occasional 1–2s increased latency while we move traffic.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien

Folks — forwarding BrightCommerce incident. Key facts: dedicated pool bc-ded-77 saw autoscale failure (quota-check timeout) -> queue growth -> per-node token exhaustion -> 5xxs and throughput loss. Customer wants quick mitigation; they asked about routing.

Suggested immediate playbook (short):
- T+0: Confirm with customer to route traffic to hosted-compatible model. If approved, apply temporary routing policy with rate smoothing. (Connor)
- T+5: Ops to manually bring up 2 standby nodes and monitor queue depth. (Monica)
- T+15: If autoscaler still failing, extend manual pool to 4 nodes and enable KV-prefetch caching to reduce token load. (Marcus)
- T+45: Root-cause debug on quota-check service + revert temporary routing once pool stable. (Irene/Aisha)

Risks: routing adds higher per-token cost and slightly increased P95 latency; manual nodes are billed to customer reserved capacity and may affect headroom for other tenants if not cleared. Recommend we offer a service credit for the impacted window.

Attached playbook (draft): surge_mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf and a short step-file temporary_routing_steps.txt. I will coordinate the customer comms once ops confirms the first two steps.

Connor

Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — dedicated pool event (bc-ded-77)

Hi Alice / BrightCommerce team —

Thank you again for your patience while we stabilized bc-ded-77. Attached is the incident digest and postmortem we promised (postmortem-digest-20270125.pdf). Summary highlights:

- Impact window: 2027-01-16 07:55–2027-01-16 09:00 PT. During that period your pool experienced autoscaler failures that prevented the expected addition of standby nodes, leading to queue growth and elevated 5xxs. Peak error rate: 12% of requests.
- Cause: a transient quota-check timeout inside the autoscale orchestration path caused a failure to provision nodes. Root cause traced to a mis-routed retry path that overwhelmed a caching layer under certain request patterns.
- Mitigation: We routed traffic to a hosted-compatible variant at T+5, manually added 2 standby nodes at T+10, and cleared the autoscaler retry-path bug by T+40.
- Customer impact: throughput reduction (~40%) and elevated latency; we estimate ~1.8 hours of effective customer impact across your service footprint.

Action items (we own unless noted):
- Redwood: Implement a circuit-breaker on the autoscale quota-check path and add synthetic checks to detect the specific cache saturation case (owner: Irene Choi) — ETA 2 weeks.
- Redwood: Update the autoscale retry policy to avoid cascading retries on quota-check failures (owner: Marcus Lin) — ETA 1 week.
- Redwood: Provide formal SLA credit calculation and statement (owner: Monica Patel) — ETA 3 business days.
- Customer: Confirm acceptance of proposed credit calculation and sign-off on scheduling a joint postmortem review in the next 10 business days.

We've also uploaded our internal runbook draft and the temporary routing steps to the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/brightcommerce-temporary-routing

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the postmortem and credit calculation.

Thanks — we'll follow up on the credit paper and the code fixes.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
